diagnosis.root_cause: Two coupled mechanisms in the baseline RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, max_depth=None, min_samples_leaf=1) drive this overfitting pattern on the 96-month series: (1) Unconstrained Tree Depth & Single-Sample Leaves — with default max_depth=None and min_samples_leaf=1 on compact monthly windows (16 to 80 observations), individual decision trees partition the feature space until terminal leaves isolate single historical months, memorizing in-sample noise (±5% monthly fluctuations) and driving Training RMSE down to ~3% of revenue; and (2) Step-Function Extrapolation Ceiling on Non-Stationary Secular Growth — TrackFlow's consolidated revenue compounds at 6% ± 3% annually (alternating 3% and 9% growth years), meaning every chronological validation fold operates in a higher nominal EUR regime than its preceding training window, and tree ensembles cannot extrapolate linear trends beyond the maximum y_train value observed during training (causing systematic peak under-prediction during November–December +25–35% surges).
diagnosis.corrective_action: Implement a two-part remediation before promoting the model to the staging environment: (1) Structural Tree Regularization — constrain tree complexity by setting max_depth=4, min_samples_leaf=2, and min_samples_split=4 (or max_features='sqrt') in RandomForestRegressor so terminal leaves average across multiple seasonal cycles rather than memorizing individual months; and (2) Causal Linear Trend Detrending — fit a causal linear trend baseline (Ridge/OLS on trend_index fitted strictly within each fold's training window) or transform the target into year-over-year relative ratios (y_t / lag_12) prior to fitting the Random Forest on the stationary seasonal residuals, eliminating the step-function extrapolation ceiling on compounding 3%–9% annual revenue growth.
